args.thought:
On-call plan (divide & conquer) for intermittent 502s in prod edge-gateway behind NGINX Ingress (eks-us-east-1):
1) Bisect by layer: determine if 502 is generated by NGINX (upstream failure) vs app (5xx) by correlating NGINX ingress controller logs and upstream status codes during deploy/scale windows.
2) Bisect by time/event: overlay spikes with deploy rollouts, HPA events, node scale-ups, and endpoints changes; narrow to a single rollout window.
3) Bisect by traffic path: compare same request path across AZs/nodes; check if failures cluster to specific nodes/pods (suggests conntrack, MTU, node pressure).
4) Check readiness/termination: verify pod readiness gates and terminationGracePeriod; ensure NGINX respects endpoint updates and that preStop/drain is configured so pods aren’t removed before connections drain.
5) Validate timeouts/retries alignment: ensure ingress proxy_read_timeout/proxy_connect_timeout and upstream keepalive align with service timeouts; confirm no aggressive retries amplifying load during scale events.
Highest-signal no-downtime prod checks (run now):
A) Inspect NGINX ingress controller logs for 'upstream prematurely closed connection', 'no live upstreams', connect() timed out, and correlate to deploy timestamps.
B) Check Kubernetes endpoints for edge-gateway during spike (rapid churn/empty endpoints) and compare with readiness transitions.
C) Sample node/pod resource & networking signals during spike: node CPU/mem pressure + conntrack drops/time_wait growth; compare failing vs healthy nodes.
